We were recommended Thatcher & Hallam for conveyancing by our estate agent.

My partner contacted them to instruct them on a Thursday and didn’t receive a response until the following Tuesday. When they did reply, the response was unhelpful. A week later, we still hadn’t heard anything further, aside from a slightly snotty email saying they were busy and asking us not to contact them. Not a great impression. As of today, they still haven’t come back to confirm.

As a result, our buyer was left waiting over a week for us simply to confirm basic conveyancer details for the memorandum of sale. This made us look disorganised and could easily have put our sale at risk.

The estate agent who originally recommended them ultimately advised us to abort and go elsewhere. The new conveyancer they recommended replied and got it sorted within an hour - and even replied out of office hours.

If they can’t be bothered to respond at the very start of the process, I dread to think how responsive they would be during the actual conveyancing. We also made it clear that we had another sale and a purchase coming up, so they’ve effectively lost out on two sales and a purchase due to being so slow, unprofessional and unresponsive in even getting themselves instructed.

I’d strongly recommend avoiding them and choosing another firm that actually wants new conveyancing customers.

We purchased a recently renovated property completed by MAINTY Group, and unfortunately our experience has been extremely concerning from the moment we moved in.
Very quickly, we identified multiple serious issues throughout the property, including:
Active water ingress, with water visibly entering the property and running internally
Mould development as a direct result of ongoing moisture
Roofing defects, despite being told that all relevant works had already been completed
Cracking and poor finish across internal walls
Flooring issues (uneven carpets and poorly installed flooring)
Faulty installations (radiator not functioning correctly, door hardware issues, general finishing defects)
The most serious concern is that water is still actively entering the house, which directly contradicts the assurances given that all water ingress issues had been addressed during the renovation.
This situation has been particularly difficult as it has occurred during winter, while my wife is heavily pregnant, and with a young child in the household. Living in a property with active water ingress and mould in these conditions is simply not acceptable.
We have repeatedly contacted MAINTY Group, shared photos and videos clearly showing water entering the property, and attempted to resolve the matter professionally.
Despite this:
The issue has not been properly resolved
We were informed that further repairs would be chargeable, even though the problems relate directly to areas previously addressed during the renovation
Requests for clear clarification of what is covered under the warranty have not been answered
A key document (the original scope of works) has still not been provided, despite multiple requests over several weeks
At no point has there been a clear, structured response or resolution plan provided.
We have documented all issues with supporting evidence (photos, videos and email correspondence), and the lack of accountability and follow-through has been extremely disappointing.
Based on our experience, we would strongly advise against working with MAINTY Group. The standard of workmanship and the lack of effective aftercare make this a high-risk choice for any property project.

2 months after buying the van the cam belt snapped on my way to work which left me stranded on the side of the road waiting for the AA.

As the van was bought with an AA warranty, the lovely AA man told me not to worry & that he would tow the van to an AA approved garage for inspection. I walked home feeling optimistic that everything would be sorted out quickly.

Once home I began making phone calls to try to hire a van for work the following day & the weekend as we were going away fishing. The AA garage called to say they couldn't do the inspection until Friday (it was Wednesday) & I needed to pay £40 for them to carry out the inspection. This I did.

I also called Family Cars to let them know what had happened & asked if there was any chance they would be willing to cover the cost of the hire van. I initially spoke to Jack who sounded quite panicked that the van had been towed to a local garage & said it should have really been brought back to them. (I'm in Cheltenham, they are in Bristol) I told him the name of the garage so he could speak to them to see what was going on & said I'd paid for the inspection but it couldn't be carried out until Friday.

My next contact was from the AA thanking me for cancelling the inspection! I hadn't, but it turned out that Jack had.

I then received 2 emails from Steve. The first saying the car would be picked up at 0800 the following day so they could carry out their own inspection. The second telling me to remove all my personal possessions from the van & leave all the documents & keys in it. I was advised that once they had the van back & inspected it they would give me a refund!!

I was quite shocked by this chain of events so called Family Cars again to clarify what was going on & spoke to steve.

He was very aggressive on the phone & showed absolutely no sympathy towards my situation. Instead he told me he didn't think I realised how damaging this could be to their business & that it could ruin them. I tired to point out that as a self employed carer I did indeed understand the impact as I had lost a day's pay & left my clients without care that day, but he brushed this off saying that my few hours of work were not as important as their business! When I tried to ask him not to belittle my job caring for the elderly Steve then launched into a tyraid of abuse telling me I was disgusting, disrespectful & that he wanted nothing more to do with me. I ended the call while Steve was still ranting.

I can only assume that there was more wrong with the van than I had been told when buying it & that Family Cars did not want the AA to inspect it & find out what.

I have been left bitterly disappointed by the whole experience & considerably out of pocket by the cost of a days pay lost,  PDF flush, oil change as the oil light came on a couple of weeks after purchase & the hire of a replacement van.

Christine

We completed on our first home in November 2024, so you can imagine how stressful it was to later find out in 2026 — when we came to sell — that the property hadn’t even been registered in our name.

We only discovered this after accepting an offer, when our new solicitors flagged it. Up until that point, we had no idea there was any issue at all.

It turns out a Land Registry requisition from October 2025 had been sent to an inactive inbox and simply wasn’t picked up. Nothing was done about it for months, and a cancellation notice was even issued — all without us knowing.

So from our perspective, everything was fine… until suddenly our sale was delayed, and we were left dealing with uncertainty, chasing for answers, and worrying about losing our buyer.

That period was incredibly stressful. Instead of being able to focus on moving forward, we were stuck in limbo trying to understand what had gone wrong and how long it would take to fix.

To be fair, once we pushed the issue and made it clear we were selling, things were dealt with quickly. But that almost makes it harder to accept, because it shows this could have been sorted much earlier if it had just been properly monitored.

What’s also disappointing is that this isn’t the first issue we’ve had. We previously raised a complaint during the original transaction due to poor communication and handling, which was upheld. Because of that, we trusted that things would be handled more carefully going forward.

Unfortunately, that doesn’t feel like what happened here.

Even in this most recent complaint, while some of the issues were acknowledged, there was no real apology for the impact this had on us — despite the stress, delay to our sale, and the position it put us in.

I completely understand that Land Registry delays can happen, but this wasn’t that. This was something being missed and left unresolved until it became a problem.

In the end it was sorted, but it caused avoidable delay, unnecessary stress, and a lot of uncertainty at a really important time for us.

We got married at St Audries Park in August 2024 and, sadly, our experience after the wedding has completely overshadowed what should have been a special occasion.

Following our wedding, a significant number of our personal belongings were not returned to us, including bespoke wedding items (custom made personalised vow books & A5 signs), gift cards and money (left in the manager’s possession), sentimental keepsakes and decorative items that had been handed over to venue staff.

We were later told that a large box of our belongings had been packed and posted back to us. However, nearly two years on, St Audries Park have still been unable to provide any evidence of this whatsoever — no tracking reference, no courier details, no dispatch confirmation, no proof of contents and no proof of delivery.

Despite repeatedly stating the items were “returned”, they have been unable to show any evidence that they were ever actually sent.

This has been the most frustrating part of the entire process. Had the venue simply accepted responsibility early on and tried to resolve matters properly, this review may have looked very different. Instead, this has involved nearly two years of chasing, repeated delays, contradictory responses and a refusal to provide any meaningful resolution.

What has been most disappointing is not just the loss of our belongings, but how poorly this has been handled since. The tone throughout has felt defensive, dismissive and focused more on avoiding responsibility than resolving the issue fairly. The board of directors have refused in person meetings and phone calls.

For a venue that markets itself as premium and specialises in weddings, we expected much better care, much better communication and much better accountability. We had to pay a £1k deposit which was very slowly returned after repeated chase calls, but the irony is it feels like we should have taken a deposit from St Audries Park for taking possession of our items in the end!

A beautiful venue in photographs, but based on our experience, be extremely cautious about leaving any personal belongings, sentimental items or anything of value in their care. We would not recommend this venue to any new couples.

Extremely disappointing, we had a fantastic meal here a couple of years ago but unfortunately it’s gone drastically downhill.

Despite being called ‘The Catch’ we were informed (after we had already ordered drinks) that crab, lobster, prawns, squid and the oysters were off the menu… had we been informed beforehand, we would’ve left.

The kids ‘linguine’ was not linguini and definitely not worth £9. The only fish left on the menu was the hake for the fish and chips which was clearly not a fresh ‘catch’.

Never leave reviews but unfortunately had to on this occasion. We appreciate that the kind manager managed to get us a walk-in table but he probably should have turned us away as the restaurant seemed to be completely struggling with the amount of customers they had.

We arrived at 6.30 and were finally asked about drinks about 15 minutes later. We decided to put our food order in then as it seemed to be more efficient (and we wanted to help the overrun staff out) but were told it wouldn't come any quicker. We waited about 40 minutes for our drinks, which we reminded our waiter about (and he seemed puzzled that they hadn't already arrived) when he gave us our starter.

The mains came about an hour and a half later, about 4 minutes before we were set to just leave. In that time, several tables just left after being paid no attention to, and several others complained. The food was overpriced for what it was (£23 for a burger, and the bun was burnt), and weirdly, a Pepsi Max cost the same as a Pepsi and a beer (all £6). At no point were we asked about allergies or if we wanted water for the table (despite having glasses).

Just a baffling experience overall. I don't like to complain as I understand it is hard to run a busy restaurant and the waiters were apologetic, but it wasn't exactly packed and the service was so random; we were given menus a second time by a different person even though we had already ordered. They seemed to be out of a lot of options (as other reviews have mentioned) and uncommunicative about wait times: we heard another table who had arrived before us (and who were so unattended to by the staff that we assumed they had finished eating and were just enjoying dessert or something) being told that their food would be another 45 minute wait on top of a 30 minute wait. Just so weird. The manager(?) did give us 10% off though.

So yeah, wouldn't go here again. Would recommend staff don't take walk-ins if they are already struggling with long wait times and tell people upfront what is and isn't available before they commit to a table.

Moderate noise
Seating type
Indoor dining area, Outdoor patio / terrace
Very Poor experience. An hour wait for food, and then food arriving before drinks. No gluten free options available when we got there despite booking in advance.

Unfortunately, based on our experience, we would not recommend this restaurant.

We visited Catch during our honeymoon in Cornwall after walking for over an hour from Watergate Bay Hotel specifically because we’d seen lobster on the menu and were really looking forward to it. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing from start to finish.

The first issue was the table location. We were seated in what was essentially a gangway between the kitchen/service area and the toilets. Staff and customers were constantly squeezing past us, the table and drinks shook every time someone brushed by, and people regularly had to stand right next to us to let others pass through. It genuinely didn’t feel like an appropriate place to seat paying customers.

The service was also very poor. Our waitress appeared completely unfamiliar with both the menu and basic customer interaction. We had to prompt her to take our order, she seemed confused by simple drink requests, and after waiting some time another waiter came over to apologise and explain that she hadn’t actually entered our food order at all because she was new.

More concerningly, at no point did anyone ask about allergies, despite this being a seafood restaurant. My wife has a nut allergy, so this is something we would normally expect staff to check routinely as part of basic service and food safety.

At that point we then discovered there was no lobster or crab available, despite these being prominently featured on the menu and the main reason we chose the restaurant. This should have been communicated immediately upon arrival, not after we’d already ordered drinks and starters. Had we known earlier, we would have gone elsewhere.

We ended up ordering fish and chips instead, but were never even told what the “catch of the day” actually was, so we had no idea what fish we were being served. The drinks also arrived in a vase-style container without glasses, which took another several minutes to appear.

The food itself was disappointing too. The batter on the fish was absurdly thick in places (close to 1cm) and very heavy. Both of us ended up peeling large amounts off, and my wife felt quite sick afterwards.

Another thing that really stood out was the salt and pepper presentation. Leaving loose salt in open shells may look aesthetically pleasing, but it’s completely impractical and honestly unhygienic, customers are effectively expected to put their hands into communal seasoning containers, which isn’t something I’d expect at any restaurant.

The only positive was that the whitebait and squid starters were genuinely nice, which is the only reason this isn’t the worst meal we’ve ever had.

Overall, this felt like a restaurant far more focused on appearance and “Instagram aesthetics” than customer comfort, communication, hygiene, safety or food quality. Very disappointing, especially during what was supposed to be a special honeymoon meal.

Visited recently as a local, bringing my dad and stepmum for a treat — it was the first time I’d seen them in over a year. The decor was really lovely and the space itself has a great feel, but unfortunately the overall experience was disappointing.

The main issue was the food not matching what’s described or shown. My linguine (photo attached) was missing multiple key elements (no lemon, pesto, chilli, capers or the advertised dollop of cream) and lacked the expected garlic flavour, quite dry and flavourless. The prawns were also mostly full of roe. My dad’s dish had similar issues — missing components and not resembling what’s advertised at all.
The chowder was the only dish that came close, although even there the prawns were mostly roe. The scallop starters were nice, but lacked any real garlic flavour.

Service was slow despite there being several staff on, (most seemed nervous) and we were the only table of three seated inside for most of the visit. We also had to ask for the main menus after being seated, as only the specials menu was on the table. We had to ask several times for butter, and there was dirty cutlery on the table which needed replacing. One of the toilet doors also had no proper handle.

There were MAJOR issues with the bill. We were initially told 10% had been taken off, which turned out to be the standard local discount, and the scallops were incorrectly priced. After a couple of adjustments (including one that actually increased the bill), it became quite difficult to follow what had been corrected. As a heads up to others, it’s worth checking your bill carefully rather than just paying!!!
The total bill was originally over £100 before the reduction, so this was by no means a cheap meal, and we ended up not staying for desserts due to the experience.

We dined in 2 other places a few days later and had a far better experience food-wise, which highlighted the difference.

The front-of-house staff were pleasant and did try to help although seemed nervous as mentioned above. Overall it felt like things weren’t flowing properly in the kitchen or with billing.

Unfortunately, this experience has put me off returning, which is a shame given the recommendations.

We purchased a Suzuki from this dealer some time ago. The salesperson came across as very confident and trustworthy, and we were persuaded to stretch to the very top of our budget based on repeated reassurances about the car’s quality.

Within the first week, we had to return the car due to issues. To be fair, these were repaired at the time, and we were reassured throughout the process. However, during both the sale and the follow-up, there was repeated mention of a £50 gift voucher in exchange for leaving a glowing review, which felt uncomfortable and, in hindsight, inappropriate.

Shortly after, and just outside of the warranty period, the engine completely failed. The car is now unusable, and we’re left around £5,000 out of pocket while still paying the finance. We’ve been unable to recover any of the losses.

Looking back, we feel we were pressured into the purchase, and the repeated incentive for a positive review raises concerns about the authenticity of other feedback. Our experience has been extremely disappointing and costly.

Customer Non Service at it's finest I am so sorry to say.

So my issue with Trevaskis Farm started a long time before today's debacle. I went for breakfast here 2 years ago and paid 16 pounds for a sausage bap and a bacon bap. I vowed I would never do this again.

So roll forward 2 years and we have family come down for the weekend. We were struggling for ideas for a late breakfast when here got bought up. I mentioned my experience but said I was happy to try again.

We booked and arrived to find this place only a third full. On the desk a late years teen is there in a an unironed shirt looking like he was being held their against his will. No good morning no hello we are straight to: do you have a booking? We did. So we get seated and the usual meal choice chatter unfolds.

I see my 8 pound baps and think I cannot go through that again. So I think about 2the big breakfast it is 16 pounds but my predicament is I do not like 4 of the 9 items. Not the restaurants fault that part is on me but what follows next isn't.

There is a section of the menu that reads:

"Please note: We do not do "swaps" on breakfast items but you may order extras if you wish."

It is then I see on the main menu Toast on its own. So to my mind using the add extra options I can order toast and add the bacon, potatoes, sausages and hogs pudding I require. It would come to 12.75 ish but at least I get plate of what I would like. At this point I am feeling foolish for not having seen this before.

A few minutes passes and the chap in the unironed shirt comes back to take our order. He takes everyone elses and gets to me and I say I would like the toast with bacon, sausage, hogs pudding and potatoes added. I tell him what it should come to and he looks me at confused and says " I dont think you can do that." I explain the menu literally states you can't swap but you can add. He says he will ask the chef so he goes off and comes back and says I can have it at the price of a breakfast and they can remove what I don't like. I explain again that the menu states that I can add to a menu item. He mumbles something about that isn't what it means and I can tell I am not going to get what I am asking for.

So I inform him he is going to make an extra 5 pound out of me on this day but In turn I will never ever go there again and will never endorse the place so down the road they will miss out on hundreds of pounds worth of sales in the future. For context our bill was around 100 pounds for 5 people and I also work in a public facing position in the local area  where people on occasion ask me about certain places.

But it seemed he was happy to die on that hill. So I gave him my order and had a good chunter to myself. A family breakfast I found dificult to enjoy.

Anyway the food comes and I am surprised to see it has not been done correctly. The chap said the food I didn't want would put on a separate plate for others to eat. Unfortunately, the beans I don't want are on my plate and there is no egg I don't want on either plate!  How can this be?!

If he had gone with my instruction of putting toast through with the additions then none of this happens more importantly I don't have to write this review!

So I eat my food, which was tasty but I just didn't really want it in the end. You should never have to get into an argument with someone in restaurant especially when by the terms of the menu I have done nothing unacceptable.

Do it for the 1 customer who has asked for it and change your menu wording. I have never negatively reviewed anyway before across multiple review platforms and I don't take pleasure in writing it but I felt so poorly about this experience that I wanted to give the full story rather than just 1 star and no wording.

You have lost a local customer forever I am afraid. I may just be a drop in the ocean but I am still a drop.

I booked a lodge 7a for myself, my husband, our two children and our dog for a six-night stay during May half term week. In the run-up to our arrival, the host told me that the lodge listing was "up with errors" but did not explain what those errors were. I asked her to confirm the booking. I received no reply. The booking continued to show as confirmed in the Airbnb system and my payment had gone through, so I reasonably understood the stay to be in place.

We arrived at 4pm, one hour after check in time, with our two children, to find another family already in occupation of the lodge.

The host then told us that the booking was showing as cancelled on her end — despite us having received no cancellation notice prior to arrival. It took around half an hour to get in touch with her and she engaged with us for approximately the first hour.Her last contact was around 6pm on the Sunday evening, after which she did not respond to any further messages.

The booking — which she had told us was already cancelled — was then formally cancelled on the system at 5:45pm, two hours and forty-five minutes AFTER our scheduled check-in time, and after she knew we had arrived to find the lodge double-booked.

We were left stranded with two young children, 7 hours from home, with no accommodation and no further communication from the host. We resolved the overnight situation ourselves through family in the area, while Airbnb has been beyond horrendous and provided no substantial solution until 10:30pm.

I would not recommend this Queenswood Holidays at all. A host who goes unreachable when a booking falls over is one thing; a host who knew in advance that there were "errors" with the listing, did not answer when asked to confirm the booking, then told us on arrival that it had been cancelled while it had not in fact yet been cancelled, is another. I wish we had read the reviews before booking, not just for what they said but the fact that Amy does not respond to any negative reviews (except one). We are now a substantial amount of money out of pocket due to needing to find last minute accommodation during half term week in an incredibly popular part of Cornwall. This was a gift voucher given by colleagues for my 60th birthday, so I feel bad as it sounds like I'm ungrateful.
I booked the table 48 hours in advance and gave card details for £20 deposit if we didn't show. I added a note to explain the reason for the visit and also that I was bringing mum after a difficult year in the hope there would be a special welcome as described in a previous review. In the description for the voucher it states:
"Please call us to reserve, so we can make sure we reserve you one of our best tables and have everything ready for your arrival."
I'm not sure why this is the system as the reality was a little more down to earth. There was no indication our table was reserved or that they had read the special request. It was noisy and our table was between the kitchen door, toilet and exit - the door was frequently left open which meant there was a constant draught. The toilet had a wet floor and a child had clearly used it before I did!
Our waiter was lovely - very responsive, polite and helpful.
The food was ok - 2 cheese sandwiches ⭐️ (finger and more pickle and rocket than cheese) 2 ham sandwiches ⭐️⭐️ 2 sausage rolls ⭐️⭐️⭐️, 2 arancinis  (not to our taste )⭐️ 2 cheese tartlets (more chutney than cheese) ⭐️2 scones ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️(lovely and fresh) with cream and jam enough for one, a selection of tray bake cakes which we brought home  - look nice enough, 2 pots of tea and finally 2 fizzy wine which we took away in coffee cups as it was lunchtime and we didn't fancy it.
I think I had higher expectations for £30 per head. When I saw the voucher I pictured table cloths, napkins, and bone china. Instead it was more like a cafe with 3 dying daffodils and a crab cake instead of a scotch egg!
I think it was very overpriced although it has given mum and I a wonderful afternoon out and so much to talk about although perhaps not for the reason intended. The reviews we read were accurate for a motorway service station - there is EV charging, covered bike shed and outdoor wash basins but we were there with very different expectations, maybe because it was our first "Sparkling afternoon tea for two". Our first and last i might add - what a shame!!

As a family with two Blue Badge holders and four neurodiverse individuals, close-proximity parking is a non-negotiable safety requirement for us. The car park was at maximum capacity with zero disabled bays available. To get my children safely inside, I temporarily parked in an empty EV charging bay.The director left a note on my windscreen and confronted me with extreme hostility. When I explicitly explained our significant accessibility needs, her responses were deeply dismissive and manipulative:

• She accused us of "hogging" the bay.

•She told a disabled family we "should have parked earlier" to get a space.

•She dismissively told us to park "round the back" and walk across the entire site.

•She prioritized the charging speed of the bay over my family's physical safety.

•She claimed "disabled bays are not required because of when the car park was built.
"This legal claim is entirely false. Under the UK Equality Act 2010, accessibility is an ongoing civil obligation. Age does not exempt Atlantic Reach from making reasonable adjustments.

Supplying a hostile confrontation instead of basic empathy or flexibility is a total failure of care.

If you require accessible facilities, hidden disability awareness, or basic customer respect, avoid this resort.

would strongly advise anyone considering Easton Bevin Block Management to think very carefully before doing so.

Residents and leaseholders at Pippets Court, Severn Beach, have experienced ongoing issues for a prolonged period, with extremely poor communication and little to no accountability from the management company.

Despite repeated emails, phone calls, and formal complaints from multiple residents, correspondence is routinely ignored. The only consistent communication we seem to receive relates to requests for additional payments and increased management fees, despite longstanding issues remaining unresolved.

One of the biggest concerns has been the ongoing roof problems. Multiple repair attempts have apparently failed over several years, yet leaseholders continue to be asked for further contributions without any clear transparency regarding previous funds or where money has been spent. Serious questions remain unanswered.

Most concerning of all is the impact this has had on residents themselves. An elderly couple at the property were assured repairs above their flat would be completed urgently, yet nothing was done. Their bedroom has since suffered severe water ingress, causing substantial damage and affecting their health and wellbeing. This situation should never have been allowed to happen.

There has also been no AGM for several years, leaving leaseholders without any meaningful opportunity to ask questions or challenge decisions. Transparency appears to be completely lacking.

Meanwhile, basic services continue to decline. Garden maintenance is minimal, communal upkeep is poor, and services such as window cleaning appear to have stopped altogether.

Overall, the level of service provided has been deeply disappointing. Residents are left chasing responses, dealing with unresolved maintenance problems, and facing increasing costs without justification or accountability.

In all honesty, they do not even deserve the one star that has to be given in order to leave this review.

If these issues continue to be ignored and no meaningful response is received, this matter will have to be escalated further with the appropriate authorities. At this stage, residents would even consider pursuing legal action given the lack of communication, accountability, and resolution.

Until there is a significant improvement in communication, transparency, and management standards, I cannot recommend Easton Bevin Block Management.

1/5 Stars: I’ve Seen More Pokémon in a Funeral Home

​To the management of The Big Sheep,
​I’m not saying your "Pokémon Bank Holiday Extravaganza" was a scam, but I’m pretty sure Team Rocket ran the marketing department and then pulled a disappearing act with our £30.

​My wife and i was lured in by the siren song of your advertisements. I pulled enough overtime to satisfy a Victorian factory owner just to get the day off, only to arrive at what can only be described as a "Pokémon themed desert."

​The "Attractions" (Or Lack Thereof)
​The Snorlax Bouncy Castle: Where was he? Did he oversleep? Was he ever even there? We spent the day looking for a giant inflatable blue cat-thing and found nothing but the crushing weight of our own regret.

​The "Professional" Vendors: Turns out, when you demand a 20% cut of earnings, professional card sellers stay home. The only "cards" I saw were the ones the staff were probably playing in the breakroom while laughing at us.

​The "Treasure" Hunt: This was less of a fun game and more of a mandatory endurance test. Scattering posters across the park like a breadcrumb trail for a marathon runner is not "family fun"—it’s a physical ordeal. My wife spent two grueling hours navigating the terrain for a "prize" that was essentially a slap in the face.

​The Loot
​Speaking of prizes, let’s talk about the "Freebies." You promised a hoard of Pokémon gold; you delivered the bottom-of-the-barrel "fun packs" usually found taped to the front of a dusty £2 magazine. My disappointment is immeasurable, and my day is ruined.

​The Lone Bright Spot:
Shoutout to the poor soul sweating in the Pikachu suit and the announcer. They were the only things actually present that belonged to the franchise. They were like the band playing on the deck of the Titanic—bless their hearts, but the ship was still under 50 feet of water.

If you’re looking for a "Pokémon experience" that involves wandering aimlessly through a field looking for things that don't exist, just go for a walk and hallucinate. It’s cheaper.

​Never again.

Review Title: $250 Lost, 3 Months of Excuses — I Had to File a Claim to Get My Money Back
I’ve been a loyal Foxy Locks customer for years, spending thousands annually, but this last experience has completely ended that relationship. I paid $250 for merchandise that I never received, and instead of stepping in as a responsible business should, Foxy Locks :Josie left me in limbo for over three months.
She repeatedly told me the package was being “held” at DHL and that only I, the customer, could resolve it. That’s absurd. As the recipient, I had no authority to search DHL warehouses, no access to their systems, and no ability to make DHL release a package they themselves couldn’t locate. But trust me, I tried I dealt with DHL reps, supervisors anybody up the chain of command I could. In reality, the parcel was lost. Period. But instead of acknowledging this and taking responsibility, Foxy Locks chose to hide behind policy.
One line from their emails summed it up: they said refunding me while the package was “available” would have been a risk. Risk? The only risk here was leaving me, the paying customer, with no product and no money. Whether they refunded me or sent a replacement, the company’s position would have been the same — down one order. But instead of protecting their loyal customer, they chose to protect themselves.
And here’s what makes it worse: I didn’t get my refund because Foxy Locks decided to do the right thing. I got my money back because I filed a claim against them and won. That’s not customer service — that’s being forced to fight for what was already mine.

The contractor had quoted the works required to Vibrant at £538 but the price I recieved from my letting agency was almost double that price!

It seems Vibrant just stick an extremely high mark up on the prices and let the landlords foot the costs!

It strongly gives the impression that prices are being artificially inflated before being passed on to landlords and the letting agencies are complicit in this too.

This prompted me to do some research on Vibrant and it seems that Connells group actually own Vibrant Energy Matters!

If your report or work is being arranged through a letting agency owned by Connells, Sequence, Countrywide I would urge you to look very carefully at the figures quoted and if you are concerned you may have been ripped off contact the company on your surveys paperwork directly and see if you can discuss the price with them, then seek legal advice about claiming back any significant over charge that you may have paid.

I have spoken with others who have had similar experiences with Vibrant and Connells and believe there is a part 2 Panorama documentary coming out soon exposing this racket by an undercover journalist within the organisation so that should be interesting.

Overall, this felt like a process designed with little regard for value or transparency. Proceed with caution.

We hired a campervan from Hi-De-Hi Campers late 2025. I hope to provide a fair review, so I would acknowledge the positive and negative aspects to my experience.

The initial phase - booking, handover, coordination and response time were  smooth. The ins and outs of the vehicle were explained, and Russell Marsden showed us the vehicle. We enjoyed the use of the campervan itself. However, there were damages to the campervan, including a signal light, but were told that they will not be a concern and reasonable wear and tear were acceptable, and we assumed that any issues would be handled fairly. So, we also made a genuine effort to return the campervan in good condition. Prior to handover, we cleaned the campervan thoroughly out of courtesy, and returned it in a tidy and presentable state.

Unfortunately, the post-hire process completely overshadowed the positive aspects of the experience. A minor scratch appeared on the table surface before we returned it, to which we acknowledge it, and then told that a further assessment would take approximately one week. We were unable to dispute the process as we had to catch a train and so the assessment was not done in our presence.

Subsequently, we were told of damages we were not aware of - top of the roof of the campervan, scratched paintwork, and that scratch on the table now requires complete replacing and he will contact someone.

Week after week of message chasers, attempts to arrange for phone and video calls, request for photos to see the damage, requst for insurance info, to be copied in email thread, contact info for third party - all to no avail. Russell responded with the generic "he is also waiting to hear back from some motorhome company for part detail" that kept us waiting for an answer. We resorted to googling motorhome companies ourselves after 3 months to get a quote for the matter. We were told that it was more common for owners to use wax to fix the scratch instead of replacing the whole table.

Another aspect which made it dodgy was that Russell said he considers selling the campervan this year, which led me to think that our deposit was used to fix the all the previous damages for him to fetch a better price.

While the campervan itself functioned adequately and the initial booking experience was positive, it was truly a harrowing experience to be renting a campervan here. Having to message every week for an update after months of waiting, lack of documentation for the damages, poor communication, contradictory reassurances, stress my family was under to get our deposit back when we had medical bills to pay... it tainted the family holiday for my wedding. The situation deteriorated to the point where we had to pursue legal avenue in order to recover our deposit — something that should never be necessary when dealing with a legitimate business acting in good faith.

Considering how good the reviews were, we were flabbergasted by the treatment from Russell/Hi-De-Hi, and would strongly advise prospective customers to ensure that all deposit arrangements, damage assessment procedures are clearly documented in writing before proceeding with a hire.

We hired a campervan from Hi De Hi Campers in October 2025. During this rental period, we liaised with the owner, Russell Marsden directly over WhatsApp.

Pros:
The booking and handover process was smooth. Russell gave a thorough walkthrough of the vehicle, and the campervan served its intended purpose for our trip. There were pre-existing issues (for example, a broken window signal light), and we were reassured these would not be charged to us. We were also told that reasonable wear and tear from normal use was expected. In hindsight, these reassurances were misleading, as the post-hire process revealed serious issues.

Cons:
We chose this company based on its positive reviews, but we were left disappointed. The post-hire damage handling was extremely poor. During our trip, a minor scratch appeared on the table surface. At handover, we were told assessment would take about a week. Instead, we had to chase for updates from October 2025 until 2 March 2026 — nearly five months later — and we are still waiting for complete paperwork regarding the issue. Documentation was severely lacking, and Russell’s communication was poor; he repeatedly avoided providing requested information.

Russell insisted the entire table must be replaced for a single scratch and made this decision before properly considering repair. He could not even get a quotation or response from the supplier, yet replacement remained the proposed solution.

Additional unverified damages were also attempted for deduction from our deposit. The standard deposit for hirers is around £1,000–£1,250, but we were asked to pay more on the basis that we were from out of state. While different risk policies may apply, this felt disproportionate and exploitative. Furthermore, Russell told us that cash payment was preferred for part of the proposed damage cost, with comments suggesting this is what business people do for tax-related reasons, raising serious concerns.

Overall, the lack of transparency, misleading reassurances, prolonged delays, poor communication, and questionable handling of the damage claim severely overshadowed the hire. While the campervan itself worked as intended, the post-hire experience has been frustrating and stressful.

We strongly advise prospective customers to ensure all deposit terms, damage assessment policies, payment methods, and timelines are clearly documented in writing before hiring from this company.

It is extremely disappointing that something that was meant to be a positive experience is ruined by a dealer like Russell...

I have been using Ocean Falmouth for my servicing needs since I bought my car 5 years ago, and for the most part have been happy with the service I received. However, over the past year or so I have noticed a steady decline in the level of service, and with my latest experience they have sunk to an all time low, and I will not be using them again.
Last winter my car developed a water leak inside on the passenger side footwell back and front. I took it in to Ocean in November and they replaced a gasket, however they either did not do this properly or they did not re-test for leaks afterwards as over the winter with all the heavy rains it leaked worse than ever, at one point filling the footwell right up to the door sill.
I took the car back to Ocean Falmouth, and because I had to go into hospital I left it with them for around 7 weeks. During this time, I received no feed-back from them, and when I contacted them I was totally shocked to find out they had ‘not had time’ to look at it! The excuse was shortage of staff and too many cars booked in; I found this quite appalling service and will not be using them again.

After reading all the positive reviews, it saddens me to leave a negative one, but the service we received from BVS was poor.
Our cat needed an urgent CT scan to confirm what our vet had found during initial tests, suspected renal cancer, which they thought had spread.
He was extremely unwell yet we were told after him being referred that they could not see him for three weeks! I rang to explain how poorly he was but was met with indifference to our plight and that our vet had apparently said the wait would be fine!
We therefore elected to be referred to Langfords vets who were nothing short of amazing,  immediately arranging a zoom meeting within 24 hours to discuss his case, before getting us an in person appointment the next working day.
Sadly, and as feared, the scan showed the cancer was terminal, could not be treated, and inspite of best efforts and palliative care, we lost him 2 weeks later.
It has taken time to write this review as he was our world, but BVS really need to review how they treat people in devastating situations such as the one we faced.

An Absolute Waste of Money – Better Off Just Redoing Your Tests Again From Scratch!

I feel completely robbed after using Patterson Law. If you are facing a license revocation, take my advice: save your thousands of pounds and just redo your theory and practical tests from scratch. It is much faster, cheaper, and less stressful than dealing with this firm's "service."

I paid a staggering £2,760 in legal fees, only to receive representation that was nothing short of embarrassing. Here is what you can expect for your money:

Zero Preparation: My assigned, rather elderly solicitor, Thomas Restell, arrived at my hearing on March 20, 2026, completely unprepared. He actually forgot to bring the supporting letter from my father, which was a vital piece of evidence for my defense.

Incompetent Advocacy: He barely defended me. He focused entirely on a "Wickens defense" and failed to mention any of the real-world implications of me losing my license. He didn't tell the judge how a disqualification would destroy my work life, my finance, or my mental health.

Poor Communication: They didn't even bother to tell me my father needed to be in court. I brought my mother instead, and when we realized the mistake, I had to rush my father to the court in a last-minute Uber. It was a total shambles.

Complete Loss: After all that money, I   still lost my license and was hit with £628 in court fines.

The Alternative: Once my license was revoked, I realized I’d been scammed by the legal process. I decided to put my mind to it and re do my theory test and after I passed I got lucky with a cancellation for a practical test, and managed to get my license back in around 6 weeks by redoing everything myself. It is entirely possible to do this if you try hard and have a bit of luck.
Don't waste your time or your hard-earned money on Patterson Law. You’re paying for a "premium" service and getting a defense that misses half the facts. Avoid them at all costs.

I was submitted to unlawful data surveillance and systemic discrimination by customer service team. Avoid at all costs!!!! Rhys explicitly stated that Starling Bank refuses to accept administrative information from my PA unless a legal agreement—specifically a Power of Attorney or a Court of Protection order—was attached. Under Section 20 of the Equality Act 2010, financial service providers have an absolute duty to provide reasonable adjustments for disabled individuals. A government-funded work PA is not legal guardianship. Equating an autonomous disabled business owner using an administrative PA to someone lacking mental capacity is patronising, legally inaccurate, and deeply insulting. It demonstrates a severe lack of disability awareness. Carys sent a response explicitly admitting to an unauthorised background investigation into my health status: "So that you don't have to repeat yourself to my colleagues in future, I have recorded the information found on your company website regarding your disability..."

Under Article 9 of the UK GDPR, health data is classified as Special Category Data. Processing this data requires an explicit, unambiguous lawful basis. I did not provide consent for Starling Bank to conduct internet surveillance on my business website, nor did I consent to the harvesting, scraping, or logging of my health profile. This action directly violates Starling’s own Privacy Notice, which pledges that you only process health data "when you tell us about a health issue" or via "clear and informed consent". Carys actively bypassed your own requirement and legal framework. She proactively weaponised data found via external search engines to build an unauthorised health profile on a customer. This is an invasive, illegal act of background profiling. It violates my fundamental right to data privacy.

A pin sleeve was wedged inside my watch bracelet end link (pictured). I couldn’t remove it - to get a new pin in. So I left it with the shop to send away to get an assessment, probably a couple of weeks for a reply (no problem). Job done.

But, was phoned after 3 days. Their statement, we can’t help you, please collect your item (odd statement for a jeweller) and very early.

Visited the shop again and showed them the issue. They told me it was part of the design and should be there. I explained, I can’t get a pin in. Can you not see? They said no. It was taken in the back while I was there, and the jeweller then sent the receptionist out to say, ‘we can’t help you, take your bracelet and leave’  (very surreal experience, and to be fair quite rude).

So my issues are: the fact I was told it’s fine, and it wasn’t, was told it would be sent away and it wasn’t, then I was told to leave, because they couldn’t fix it, purely because they aren’t actually jewellers.. as I realised face-to-face with the actual jeweller who was completely clueless.

Noticed the £23 per gram sign for 9ct gold outside Chloe’s Jewellers — mainly because it’s been exactly the same every time I’ve passed for months, which already says a lot.

Went in to double check it wasn’t outdated and was told, confidently, that’s their “scrap price”. Genuinely made me laugh. It was said in a way like that’s just how gold works everywhere, like the rest of the world hasn’t got access to a live market price or something.

For context, as of April 2026, most places are paying around £30–£38 per gram, and even straightforward postal buyers are up at £30-£40 per gram.

What made it even more surreal is that £23/g is basically back in the territory of when scrap 9ct gold was last that low — around the 2020–2021 period, before gold prices properly climbed. So seeing it still sitting there in 2026 like nothing’s changed is wild.

So hearing “that’s scrap price” with that level of certainty was honestly the funniest part — because that’s just not how it works in the real world. Scrap gold isn’t a fixed local guess, it tracks the global price of gold.

If you know what your gold is worth, this won’t be the place you sell it. If you don’t, that sign probably does exactly what it’s meant to.

Reply:

I understand there are costs involved — every gold buyer has them. What’s impressive is how the rest of the country seems to land around £30–£40 per gram… while yours has been £23 for months and still counts as “regularly reviewed”.
That’s what made me laugh when it was called “scrap price” — said with such confidence you’d think the global gold market had been cancelled locally.
If £23 is the result of all those “factors”, I can only assume the review process involves not looking at the gold price.
Appreciate the response though — it did give me another laugh 👍

Whilst walking around, we spoke to a lovely young man who was extremely pleasant and helpful and once we had finished selecting our plants, we went to the check-out where we were greeted by two lovely young girls who were also extremely polite and friendly.

We hadn't realized (maybe stupidly) that the long green table in front of us, which was bordered by wood, was actually a conveyer belt. Her answer was 'of course, no problem' and she began to scan our items.
The next thing we knew was an extremely angry male individual shouting at us in a very aggressive manner, ordering us to unload our plants and place them on the green table, which turned out to be a conveyor belt.
The man then came towards us shouting at both myself, my husband and the poor girls serving us. shouting 'Get your plants on here, get your plants on here'!
My husband, who was completely in shock (as were we all), asked this man why the young lady couldn't scan them on the trolley?
The man's strange response was that 'we could charge you £200.00' - An extremely odd thing to say, as we knew how much we had spent and that we would be given a receipt.
My husband said to the man 'well, you've certainly made your point to all of us haven't you'. The man murmured something inaudible and strode off.

I booked this restaurant for my birthday dinner, as it is highly rated and Michelin-recognised. I made the reservation two weeks in advance, clearly noting that it was a birthday celebration and requesting a beach-view table.

Upon arrival, carrying cakes and a flower bouquet, I informed a staff member of my reservation. They appeared confused, and it quickly became clear that our table had been given away to another couple. Despite having a confirmed booking, we were asked to wait outside in the cold and were only given a blanket. This was already disappointing, as a reservation should guarantee a table—especially for a special occasion.

After some time, we were called back in and told they had “moved things around” to accommodate us. This did not feel acceptable, as we should not have needed last-minute rearrangements for a booking made well in advance. We were then seated at a cramped table right next to the bar, surrounded on all sides by other tables and constant staff traffic.

Meanwhile, the beach-view table we had specifically requested was given to other diners who were not celebrating any occasion. This made the experience even more frustrating. The seating arrangement also made it nearly impossible to take any photos without strangers in the background, which was particularly disappointing given it was a birthday celebration.

While the food itself was decent, it was noticeably overpriced for the overall experience. What stood out most was the lack of care for special occasions and poor handling of reservations. For a restaurant with this level of reputation, I expected far better service and organisation.

Unfortunately, this experience significantly impacted what should have been a special evening. I would not recommend this restaurant for celebrations, as even booking well in advance does not seem to guarantee the experience you request. I have had far better and more thoughtful service at places far less renowned.

Pretty disappointed with how this event is handled overall. It just feels a bit all over the place, and communication isn’t great, which makes things more frustrating than they need to be.

The ticket situation is a bit of a pain as well. If your plans change, there’s not much flexibility, and actually passing tickets on isn’t as straightforward as you’d expect. Tickets aren’t cheap for most people either, so being stuck with them when something comes up is a pretty big issue.

Tried reaching out to Rock Oyster Festival 2026 for some help but didn’t hear anything back, which didn’t exactly help the situation. It seems like getting a response can be a bit hit and miss.

On top of that, it doesn’t always feel like great value for money — queues can be long, it gets pretty crowded, and some of the basic stuff doesn’t quite keep up with the number of people there.

Overall, it’s a nice idea and the setting is great, but the way it’s run just doesn’t quite live up to expectations.

Had to pull out of attending this event unexpectedly, which is unfortunate but one of those things. What’s been far more disappointing is how difficult it is to pass tickets on.

The event’s website points you toward using Tixel as the official resale route, but in practice that doesn’t really work. You can’t actually list anything without a PDF ticket, and those aren’t issued until right before the event. By then, it’s unrealistic to expect anyone to buy them.

Tried getting in touch with Rock Oyster Festival 2026 for some guidance, but didn’t hear anything back. That lack of communication just adds to the frustration.

As it stands, there doesn’t seem to be any practical way to recover the cost once plans change, which feels like a pretty significant gap in the process.

I purchased £450 worth of tickets for the 2026 event but am unfortunately no longer able to attend. While I understand and accept the no-refund policy, the lack of a workable resale option has been very frustrating.

The Rock Oyster website directs customers to use the authorised resale platform, Tixel. However, Tixel requires a PDF version of the tickets in order to list them, and Rock Oyster does not issue these until one week before the event. This effectively prevents any realistic opportunity to resell tickets in advance.

I have contacted Rock Oyster twice to seek clarification or assistance and have not received any response. As things stand, I appear to have no viable option other than to absorb the full £450 loss.

Given the lack of response to direct enquiries, leaving a review feels like the only way to highlight this issue and seek some form of resolution.

Very dishonest organisers: when headliner Sophie Ellis-Bextor cancelled they just put a random dj instead without offering any compensation as every other festival does. When I contacted them on Facebook regarding it they blocked me. Definitely don't recommend.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m not sure whether this review applies to Orbital10 Yeovil or Allen Computer Services, because both businesses seem to be registered at the same address, so I honestly don’t know which company we spoke to.

I visited the shop on Wednesday with a MacBook that had been spilled on with a very small amount of coffee with milk. The computer was still turning on and making the startup sound, but then immediately shutting itself off. You could only see the Apple logo for about two seconds.

At the shop, we were told that the computer was completely dead, all data was lost, and can't be recovered due to the SDD being soldered onto the motherboard. As I had very important data on my laptop I specifically asked: “So there’s absolutely NOTHING that can be done to recover the data?” The response was: “No, NOTHING can be done, but you can leave the laptop with us for diagnostics for £40.00 to see if we can get it running, but it will have to be formatted, so all data will be lost nonetheless.'

We left.

I started searching online and found MacBook-repairs. I shipped the laptop the very same Wednesday (for fast track diagnostic at a cost of £50.00) and by Friday the laptop was already back with me, fully repaired, with ALL data recovered and intact. The total cost was £290.00 including fast track diagnostic, getting rid of the liquid and replacement of the lid sensor and audio jack.

Do you genuinely realise how much trouble such inaccurate and careless diagnoses can cause people? I could have just believed you and deal with the big trouble of losing the data. Do you understand how important the data on someone’s drive may be? Does any of that matter to you at all?

If you simply don’t know how to repair something, wouldn’t it be better to say so and refer customers to someone who can help, instead of telling them their request cannot be sorted? What exactly is the purpose of giving customers completely false information like this?

I understand that I should have had a proper backup, and unfortunately in this case I only had a partial one, but with all due respect, I genuinely feel misled.

I DO NOT recommend this shop.

Even after we explained that she struggles in medical settings and has anxiety, he repeatedly demanded to know “why” and appeared unwilling to accept our explanation, as though he expected a “better” reason. What upset us most was the way the dentist spoke to both of us. I would like to add that neither of us are confrontational people. Making this a more upsetting experience. My daughter was extremely upset witnessing the aggressive and dismissive way I was spoken to, and I can honestly say I have never experienced such unprofessional behaviour in a healthcare setting.
Patients should be treated with dignity, respect and compassion. Sadly, this appointment showed none of those qualities. We left feeling upset and humiliated, and we will never return to this practice.

I will not be returning and would not recommend this practice to anyone, to save you from meeting this horrible man.

I rarely leave reviews, but this experience has been unacceptable from start to finish.
I instructed Shergroup to enforce a High Court writ. From the outset, communication was poor. I received little to no meaningful updates unless I repeatedly chased, and even then responses were inconsistent. I was passed between staff and promised callbacks that did not happen.
Enforcement eventually succeeded and the debtor made payment by card on 9 April 2026. I was advised the funds would clear within 3 to 5 working days. However, I was not proactively updated when this happened. I had to chase Shergroup on 16 April 2026 to ask what was happening, and only then was I told that the funds had actually cleared into their client account on 14 April 2026.
It was also only after I chased that I was then informed, for the first time, that the funds would be held for a further 28 days. This had never been explained at the outset and no clear legal basis was provided. There is no stay of enforcement in place and no formal application to set aside has been served.
At the point of writing, my funds remain withheld despite enforcement being complete and despite the money having already cleared into their account. The delay, poor communication and lack of transparency have caused unnecessary and avoidable financial stress.
For a regulated firm handling High Court enforcement, the standard of communication and client handling has fallen well below what should reasonably be expected.
Based on my experience, I would not recommend this firm.

Update after the reply:  In response to the owner’s reply, I need to clarify a few factual points.
I have not spoken to anyone called “Sue”, and I do not know who that refers to. Since last week, I have not received any meaningful update unless I have chased repeatedly.
I have not had a consistent point of contact. I am repeatedly told someone will deal with the issue, then communication changes again. This lack of continuity and follow‑through has been a constant problem throughout.
I was informed in writing that funds would be held for 28 days, not 14, and this was only explained after I chased following clearance. This was not explained at the outset.
For a firm acting as High Court Enforcement Officers, the level of communication, clarity, and consistency I have experienced has been extremely poor.

Make sure you have correct contact numbers instead of frightening a person into having an angina attack because you had the wrong number.  I was initially told I couldnt speak to anyone without a reference number. I advised I hadn't got one and he put the phone down on me twice. Do better.

£15 entrance fee for adults to the permanent exhibition is digusting. In London the Tate Modern, Tate Britain, National Gallery, National Portrait Gallery all have free permanent exhibitions. What is the point of this gallery if entrance to it is only for the wealthy? This latest visit to St Ives I did not pay to go into the galleries because it was too expensive but in 2021 I did visit when it was half this price (still too much imo) and found the permanent exhibition pretty underwhelming and not that extensive. The building itself poorly signposted to know exactly what door even to enter the building and though it seems it was once a magnificent hotel it is now quite bland externally with opportunities for greenery completely passed up and ugly stainless steel railings. Next to the Museum is arguably the ugliest apartment building in the whole of St Ives with it's charmless off the peg stainless steel and glass balconies.

St Ives is a fantastic location with amazing light and sea views and beautiful beaches. The town is now somewhat ruined with doubtless very few places for the local people who work in the cafes, restaurants and shops to live. One street of old fishermans' cottages on the lead into the town from the train station is now entirely air bnbs. Everything here seems to be about rinsing tourists and Tate St Ives is no exception whereas it should be somewhere for locals and visitors alike can enjoy a permanent exhibition for free as they do in London.

I’m currently on holiday in St Ives and I have never thought I would give such a bad review on the cafe @tate st Ives. Me and my husband went into gallery hoping we could get a nice coffee. As my phone’s battery was running low I have asked nice lady at the counter if she could put my phone on charge. She said, she can’t. Not a problem, I suspected there might be liability issue as things get stollen. Totally get that. Then I saw a plug in the corner on the wall, didn’t think anymore of it and stared walking towards it. Put my plug in and then next thing I know this other blond lady jumped out with two ponytails raising her voice at me saying ‘You can’t use the plug here!’ (oh, sorry I didn’t realise there was a police patrol in a cafe and since when are we raising voice at customers? I thought those days are in the past, well clearly not). It did shock me a little and I was taken aback by her reaction. ‘You can’t use your charger!’ She continued in raised voice and which point she got a little red. ‘ It must be PAT tested, it’s legislation.’ I responded calmly ‘As far as I am aware it’s not a mandatory requirement anymore.’ She responded again raised voice ‘Well it is here,  you can’t use it cause entire building might get cut out. Unless your charger is PAT tested.’ I completely understand that too. Company policy, not a problem with that but not in a world a customer should be spoken to in such poor manner. It even got attention of other customers in the shop. It was embarrassing and there was no need for that….and then I got served this fake scone (see photo).
Clearly the waitress had an incomplete training in legislation (new electrical equipment do not need testing in the first 2 years). Additionally no training in customer service. Don’t get me wrong I don’t require special treatment. I’m an easygoing person. One thing I will not tolerate is bad manners, specially in such a nice and posh place. Note to management. I suggest you educate your staff properly on legislation rather that asking them to quote stuff without full understanding and most of all customer service. Businesses cannot survive long term without this kind of training. It has spoiled my day to be fair.

Extremely disappointed with the bouquet supplied.

We specifically asked for a replication of a sentimental wedding bouquet for our anniversary, and were assured it could be recreated closely. The original bouquet was defined by white hydrangea, snapdragons, craspedia and eucalyptus — yet none of these appear to have been included, aside from the white roses.

Instead, an entirely different arrangement was supplied using substitute filler flowers that completely changed the look and feel of the bouquet.

If substitutions were necessary, that should have been communicated beforehand — especially when the entire purpose of the order was to recreate a very specific wedding bouquet with sentimental importance.

What makes this even more disappointing is that the bouquet was for our anniversary on Monday, meaning it is now too late to source an alternative elsewhere.

Sadly, this felt less like a careful recreation and more like a generic white bouquet put together with whatever stock was available.

​I have now paid the £34.99 strictly under protest and duress to stop this harassment and protect my position. I have requested a Deadlock Letter and will be taking this case to the Ombudsman (CISAS) to reclaim the money.
​I am very disappointed in these bullying practices. I would advise anyone looking for a broadband provider to stay away. Since they started acquiring smaller ISPs, they have clearly become a company that cares more about squeezing money out of people than providing fair service.

Avoid UK Carbody Ltd in Avonmouth, Bristol

Excellent Bodywork, Atrocious Administration and Communication
I wish I could give this review two separate scores: one for the actual bodywork repair and one for everything else. Unfortunately, the “everything else” has been so bad that it completely overshadows the good parts.

The quality of the bodywork repair and valet was excellent. The panels, paint, and finish were done to a very high standard – no complaints there at all.
However, the administration, communication, and overall service have been truly atrocious.

My wife has been without her car since the end of January after our insurance company instructed UK Carbody Ltd to carry out the repairs following an accident.

•  We were told to drive the car to their premises for inspection, my wife thought the loud noise when driving was air passing through the hole in the door. So thought it was safe to drive.

•  After the first inspection, they contacted us to say it needed to be done again because the original one wasn’t completed correctly.

•  When dropping the car off for repair I told told her that the noise she suspected to be air sounded more like a wheel bearing. My wife specifically mentioned that she suspected the noise was a wheel bearing and was told not to worry they will check everything. They diagnosed the bodywork as “cost effective” to repair.

•  The bodywork was repaired and the car valeted beautifully, but the loud noise from the wheel bearing remained exactly the same after the accident. We reported it immediately.

•  UK Carbody then said the bearing is noise was “age related” because the car is 10 years old. This ignores the fact that the car had done only 50,000 miles, VW states wheel bearings typically last around 100,000 miles, none of the other bearings have failed, and crucially – there was no noise at all before the accident.

The car is now off the road and unroadworthy. We have had to escalate this through the insurance ombudsman and involve legal representation.

If your insurance company directs you to use UK Carbody Ltd for repairs, do not accept it without serious hesitation. Insist on an alternative repairer if possible. The visual repair work may be excellent  but the complete lack of proper process, communication, and willingness to address related damage makes the whole experience a nightmare.

I would not recommend this company based on our experience.

Don’t use this company

Booked and paid for a 10 person apartment, arrived and received a 8 person apartment.

Once we contacted them saying there had been a mistake we were offered £100 and I quote directly from the email - “We understand that you were told incorrect information; however, the apartment does sleep all 8 of you” (Lucy customer service) what kind of customer service is that? Not a single attempt was made to put us in the room we booked. We were told by the hotel that there was going to be single rooms coming available that we could move 2 members of our group into but said it had to be approved by Heidi. Heidi didn’t move us.

We were a group of 8 adults who specifically booked a 10 person room to give us extra space and privacy for on our 7 day holiday. We didn’t want two full grown men having to share a tiny sofa bed!! There is a difference between refunding us what we over paid for the 10 person room and actually compensating us for the mistake we had to deal with.

I do not recommend this company.

We chose to travel with Heidi over February half term - our holiday was an expensive disappointment with v poor customer service - 6 weeks now since we returned and despite Heidi initially offering me £300 compensation they have neither paid this out or even provided a response to my follow up correspondence. If you book with Heidi be prepared for a lot of hard work and hidden costs - for us this included an additional £400 for luggage which we were unaware of until check in en route to the airport (luggage not included - who doesn't need luggage on a ski holiday?!). Poor transfer times and a drop off/collection point a 25minute walk from our accomodation - challenging with three children in our party under 11. Pick up on the return was at 4am despite flight not leaving until midday - this involved us having to walk 25 minutes along a dark road in the middle of the night with small children while struggling with our luggage and felt quite unsafe. Heidi offered to pay for a taxi to the collection point - had they researched the area they would know that no taxi driver in Bourg St Maris is prepared to get up at 3.30am to drive us a mile down the road! Ski hire option from Heidi was no where near the slopes so after speaking with them we made our own arrangements but as newcomers to Les Arcs didn't realise ski lockers were booked up 9 months in advance - we booked our holiday 12 months in advance it would have been helpful if they'd mentioned this and we could have made arrangements. Instead we had no choice but to lug our own and our childrens ski equipment to and from the hotel to the funicular (25minute walk) then up and down the funicular every day - this almost broke us. As 'ski specialists' why are they recommending this hotel to families with young children? I struggle to see what value booking with Heidi added to our holiday, the holiday seemed good value when booking but don't be fooled, once I added up what we ended up spending I realised we could have stayed half board at a ski in - ski out hotel with crystal and it would have been hassle free. We won't be making this mistake again!

I rarely leave negative reviews, but our experience at Belushi's was so poor that I feel people should know what to expect.
We initially tried calling multiple times to confirm a booking, but nobody ever answered the phone. I booked online instead, but never received a confirmation email, so I popped into the venue beforehand just to make sure the booking actually existed.

When we arrived, nobody acknowledged us at all. Staff were gathered around the bar chatting amongst themselves and we genuinely felt like we were interrupting them by asking for help. One bar staff member told us to knock on the office door ourselves to get the manager. I explained that I felt uncomfortable doing that and that staff should really handle it instead. It then turned out the manager was outside on the terrace enjoying a vape and a pint.
The staff member did eventually confirm that our booking existed.

We returned that evening for the quiz night and things somehow got worse. The tables were sticky to the point that the quiz sheets were difficult to peel off the surface. Again, staff made no effort to acknowledge or engage with customers.
We were initially served by the only female member of bar staff and ordered an Appletiser, which was fine, alongside a Long Island Iced Tea that tasted absolutely nothing like it should. We politely approached the bar and asked the ginger-haired barman if it could be changed, but were bluntly told there was nothing they could do because it “would have been made to spec”.
Eventually, the same girl who made the drink came back to the bar, tasted it herself, and agreed that it didn’t taste right. To her credit, she replaced it with a glass of house wine instead.

We had originally planned to order desserts and more drinks, but no menus were ever offered and, considering the poor cleanliness and complete lack of customer care, we decided not to waste any more money there.
There were also staff drinking behind the bar throughout the evening. The long ginger-haired male staff member with braces was particularly unprofessional and by the end of the shift appeared intoxicated himself before continuing the celebrations afterwards with a group of friends.

I genuinely struggle to see how this place is making money. In the current climate, where hospitality venues are struggling, the attitude from staff seemed far more focused on having a free piss-up with friends than actually running a business properly. The entire team came across as unapproachable and unprofessional. Having since looked through other reviews, this unfortunately appears to be a recurring theme.
I would avoid this place entirely, which is a shame because the sea view itself is lovely.

I have been a loyal customer of Masala Bazar Bristol since 2023, which makes this experience even more disappointing.

In January 2026, I received my first ever letter regarding a £170 parking charge. Prior to this, I had never received any ticket, warning, or communication, despite the alleged incident being from almost two years earlier.

What is even more frustrating is that I was a legitimate customer at the time. I clearly remember providing my vehicle registration in-store, as requested by staff, so I was under the impression that parking was authorised.

The letter I received contained no clear evidence, and when I contacted the parking company to explain the situation, my correspondence was completely ignored.

Following legal advice, I approached the shop manager, who assured me that the issue would be resolved and that I should not worry. Unfortunately, despite this reassurance, three months later I received a court letter stating that I now owe the money.

This situation is extremely stressful and unfair. As a loyal customer, I did not expect to be chased for a parking charge two years later, especially when I followed the process given by the store.

Due to this experience and the lack of proper support or resolution, I will not be shopping at Masala Bazar again.

I strongly advise others to be cautious when using the parking facilities.

I just want to warn others about their car park. There are cameras and a strict 10-minute limit, which isn’t made clear enough. I stayed for around 20 minutes and ended up getting a £170 charge.

I tried to resolve it by speaking to staff, but they told me the manager wasn’t available and refused to help. Later, I found out the case had gone to court without proper communication, and now I’m being asked to pay £270.

This feels very unfair and poorly handled. Be careful if you park there—make sure you’re aware of the time limits, or you could end up in the same situation.
