On Saturday 25th April I come to the Cooper Alan concert. Unfortunately before the event I got an injured knee. I had to come to the concert on my crutches due to this as I did not wish to miss this concert. I was grateful that I was able to gain early access when I was seen in the queue waiting to get in but I was not advised on the seating outside the stage room. Therefore I was still having to stand around for the duration of 4 hours. I was not provided a seat a was a risk of further injury due to this. Thankfully there was some nice ladies who stood around me to make sure I did not fall as I shouldn't of been left without a seat. The gentleman in the accessibility area did allow me to sit on a chair when someone stood out of the room for a moment. This was because of the ladies making it noticed that I was on crutches and I should not be expected to stand for 4 hours. It was very noticeable that only 4 people in that accessibility area was actually unable to stand up. 2 of the people stood till the show started and then stood in between acts. 1 person had 2 carers for her and she only had adhd and autism (as one of the carers told me). This area is supposed to be for those who are unable to stand due to injury or have mobility issues with proof. Any mental health/invisible disability is not included in this. This has stopped a lot of people who have mobility issues attending this concert and that is unfair. It also stopped myself from gaining a seat because of my injury which caused me to leave the concert early. A lady that was in a wheelchair was not in the accessiblilty area as she was unable to book sat next to the area instead due to all of these people that could of stood in this concert. If you wish to accommodate those with mental health and invisible disabilities then you can do this buy having a less crowded corner for these people to stand as the do not need a seat to attend an event. I was also unable to call ahead of time to advise the staff as you are unable to call at weekends and can only call during the week. If I was not injured I probably wouldn't of noticed these issues and would of given a great review as the staff were extremely friendly, Building was clean and I had a great time for the amount I could stay.

I brought my car here for an MOT and already when I was booking the appointment, I found it strange that they asked me to make sure the boot was empty and that I bring the wheel nut locking key with me in case the car required repairs (no one had ever required this for any previous MOT anywhere for obvious reasons, it’s an MOT booking, not a repair booking — but ok).

Fast forward to the MOT — instead of simply passing or failing my car, they came up with a list of issues, including such absurd ones as non-reflective number plates (provided by the manufacturer and never an issue in previous MOTs) and side indicators that were supposedly not yellow enough (also original from the manufacturer and never flagged in previous MOTs), before suggesting work on the front brakes, claiming there was an issue — serious enough to fail the MOT, yet minor enough to fix immediately, according to them.

They supposedly checked the brakes and concluded that the front pads needed replacing because they had too much rust and instead of fixing/replacing them, they charged me for a “diagnosis” and told me to book in for the replacement and then come back for another MOT.

I consider the entire visit unprofessional and dishonest on their part and of course, I never went back there. I had the brakes replaced elsewhere, where parts and labour cost me £85— almost the same amount they charged me just for the supposed diagnosis (£70). The new garage that carried out the replacement (AA approved) told me that although there was some rust, this is normal when a car has been left unused for a period of time (which was the case for me) and there was no real need to replace the brakes…in other words, unnecessary work and cost.

But this isn’t about the money. It’s about the fact that they don’t seem to act in the customer’s best interest or aim to solve the problem but rather to take advantage or that they are simply amateurs who don’t know what they’re doing.

Either way, if anyone is looking for an honest, reliable, customer-focused and professional garage, this is definitely not the place I would recommend.

one_star_reviews.text:
We registered with Marlow Vets in January 2025 and were advised by Carrie, the vet, that our dog’s regular injection would be charged at a £22.50 injection fee plus the cost of medication. This was the consistent fee we were charged from then until now.

At our most recent appointment, my husband attended with our dog for the same routine treatment. We were not informed of any change in pricing at the time, and there was no discussion of increased costs. We were later invoiced £60 with no prior warning or explanation at the point of treatment. The practice also attempted to claim directly from my insurance without my knowledge; my insurer rejected this and contacted me to inform me. I was told by reception that “Glen is more expensive” and there were repeated references to “Glen this, Glen that,” which I found unhelpful and unprofessional. I also had to ask who Glen was, as I was not familiar with the name, and was told he was the owner, Mr Marlow.

I then requested a phone call from Mr Marlow; however, this was refused. Instead, I received a written email response which I found rude in tone. In that email, I was instructed to contact the practice manager, Jean Clement, if I had further queries. However, no contact details were provided. When I called reception to ask for her details, staff were unable to confirm who she was or where she was based.

In the same email, I was also informed that I could no longer attend the Undy branch and would need to travel to Chepstow for future appointments, and that the practice would no longer accept direct insurance payments. This would mean I would be required to pay upfront and reclaim from my insurer, including for my next appointment which was due in 3 days’ time.

This was the first time I had been made aware of any change to the insurance payment process. To clarify, I spoke with Pat at Chepstow and Jan at Undy. Neither were aware of this change in procedure, and both confirmed they had previously processed my insurance without issue, raising concerns that this was not a properly communicated policy change.

Jan advised she would try to seek further clarification. After this, Mr Marlow called me later that evening. He began the call by stating I had “a brief 5 minutes” of his time as he had been working since 9am and should have finished an hour earlier. When I attempted to explain the situation, I was repeatedly cut off and told, “I don’t have time for the ins and outs, I’ve already emailed you, what more clarification do you need.”

I explained that his decision to remove direct insurance payments appeared to be a reaction to me questioning the £60 charge and the lack of transparency in pricing. When I queried the lack of transparency around fees and reminded Mr Marlow of Royal Veterinary College guidance requiring clear and transparent pricing, I felt this was dismissed and not taken seriously. I was also told to “thank the government for increasing my staff’s wages.”

During communication with Mr Marlow, I was also told that he is the only vet in the area who does not charge a processing fee for insurance claims. After speaking with five other vets in the surrounding area, I would strongly disagree with this statement.

I also believe there is a need for improvement in how communication is handled, particularly in how clients are spoken to, with greater emphasis on politeness, respect, and professionalism, along with adherence to Royal Veterinary College guidance on transparent communication of fees.

Due to the lack of transparency around pricing, inconsistent communication between staff and branches, refusal of a direct call initially, the handling of both invoicing and insurance, and the unprofessional and dismissive manner in which I was spoken to by Mr Marlow, we have now moved our dog’s care to another veterinary practice where communication and costs have been clear and consistent from the outset.

There are plenty of alternative veterinary practices available. It takes years to build a reputation, and only seconds to damage it.

one_star_reviews.text:
My friend and I were renting a flat in the Downend area through a company called Intire. We were happy with the service they provided. Then that was switched to Chase Buchanan and things went down hill. Within months, they notified us that 'the landlord' had decided to increase our rent by 30%. I was in a low paid job & my friend had recently lost her job so it would have been a struggle to afford that. After some discussions, it was agreed that it would be reduced to 'just' a 15% rise. Still a struggle but we managed. About 10 moths later, they informed us - BY EMAIL - that the landlord had decided to sell the flat & that we had to get out. There was no chance of us affording to live together elsewhere and, as we were getting zero help from Chase Buchanan, we had to separate. They also charged us £300 (+ VAT) to have the place deep cleaned after we left when the flat was far from clean when we moved in 6 years earlier.
Some staff were helpful at times but I found it very unprofessional to be told that we were being evicted by email.
The only good thing to come out of this is that we'll never have to make use of the services again.
